newsitem.title: DENMARK: Quiet Danish bonds dip slightly, yield curve wider.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Danish bonds dip slightly, yield curve wider.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped a little and the 10-year yield gap with Germany widened in a quiet market on Monday, with the trend expected to continue.

"The weaker dollar has taken the pressure off short-term paper as fears of a German rate hike diminish. We foresee no Bundesbank repo change tomorrow, the focus is now on FOMC and Buba's council session on Thursday," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 closed down 0.02 point from the start at 112.50, yielding 6.08 percent. The seven percent 2007 bond, the new benchmark on September 1, ended 0.05 point lower at 105.40, with yield at 6.27 percent.

Turnover in the 2006 and 2007 papers was 2.3 and 1.7 billion crowns respectively. The 2006's September future was untraded at 112.32 while the six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.17 point to 91.23.
The crown traded at 3.8085 per mark at the close, up a smidgen from around 3.8090 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened two basis points to 62.
